andhraPradesh.headline: TTD launches AI/VR pilgrim centre, electric buses, insurance and digital services at Tirumala
facts: TTD opened the Healing and Devotion Experience Centre at Vaikuntam Queue Complex-1, with AI/VR content, guided meditation and staff training.
The Durlabha Darshan experience uses a 13-minute, 3D 360-degree VR film featuring temple rituals and services.
TTD launched 32 donated electric buses; it said free bus numbers would rise from 18 to 50 and daily trips from 300 to 810.
A TTD-LIC group insurance scheme provides ₹2 lakh life cover to devotees and Srivari Sevaks for up to four days, with TTD paying the premium.
The Nandakam app was launched for maintenance issues across 7,043 accommodation rooms; a renovated four-floor Sri Venkateswara Museum with 14 galleries and over 8,000 artefacts was also opened.
andhraPradesh.summary: On 16 September, TTD inaugurated a package of pilgrim-service initiatives combining digital interpretation, public transport, insurance and accommodation maintenance. The official release described the launches as intended to improve devotee safety, convenience and spiritual experience at Tirumala.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Temple administration, cultural heritage interpretation, e-governance and technology-enabled public services.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the Tirumala Healing and Devotion Experience Centre, Durlabha Darshan VR, Nandakam app, 32 electric buses and the ₹2 lakh TTD-LIC group cover.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how digital tools and accessible cultural interpretation can improve pilgrim services, while examining service reliability, inclusion and safeguards in technology-enabled public administration.
andhraPradesh.apLink: All initiatives were launched by TTD at Tirumala in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.

andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh gives in-principle approval to 14 Urban Challenge Fund proposals worth ₹5,912 crore
facts: The State gave in-principle approval to 14 urban infrastructure proposals with a combined estimated cost of ₹5,912 crore for submission under Phase II of the Urban Challenge Fund.
The Andhra Pradesh Urban Finance and Infrastructure Development Corporation (APUFIDC) was designated as the State’s nodal agency for the fund.
The proposals were submitted by the Engineer-in-Chief (Public Health) and forwarded to the State government through APUFIDC.
The approval is for the State’s proposal pipeline; it does not establish that the Centre has sanctioned the projects or released funding.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State’s in-principle approval advanced 14 urban infrastructure proposals for consideration under Phase II of the Urban Challenge Fund. The reported figure is a proposed project cost, not a confirmed central grant or completed investment.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Urban local bodies, municipal infrastructure finance and centre-state development programmes.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: AP’s Phase-II Urban Challenge Fund pipeline: 14 proposals, ₹5,912 crore combined cost, with APUFIDC as nodal agency; distinguish state in-principle approval from central sanction.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how urban infrastructure funds can combine public support and local financing, and the need to assess municipal debt capacity, project bankability and equitable service delivery.

andhraPradesh.headline: AP Gazette notifies withdrawal of 8 acres 65 cents of grazing-ground land in Chittoor for an industrial park
facts: AP Gazette Extraordinary No. 680, published on 16 September, notified withdrawal of 8 acres 65 cents of grazing-ground poramboke land in Pogurupalle village, Gudupalle mandal, Chittoor district.
The notification cites Section 58(2) of the Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Act, 1994, and identifies establishment of an industrial park as the purpose.
The order is G.O.Ms.No.121 of the Panchayat Raj and Rural Development Department, dated 15 September 2026.
The notification does not specify an industrial-park company, investment amount, job estimate or construction schedule.
andhraPradesh.summary: The State notified a change in the status of specified grazing-ground poramboke land in Gudupalle mandal for an industrial-park purpose. The gazette notice establishes the land-use action, not that an industrial park has been built or that investment or employment has materialised.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Common lands and poramboke classification, Panchayat Raj powers, and industrial land-use planning.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: G.O.Ms.No.121: 8 acres 65 cents at Pogurupalle, Gudupalle mandal, Chittoor; issued under Section 58(2) of the AP Panchayat Raj Act, 1994.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine the trade-off between industrial land allocation and protection of village commons, including transparent procedure, local consultation and livelihood impacts.

andhraPradesh.headline: AP High Court directs consideration of temple junior assistants for Executive Officer Grade-III posts by seniority
facts: In a common order in W.P. Nos. 16954, 16441 and 22986 of 2024 and 9293 of 2025, the Andhra Pradesh High Court allowed the petitions by temple junior assistants seeking appointment by transfer to Executive Officer Grade-III posts.
The Court directed the authorities to consider the petitioners’ cases according to their seniority under the applicable service rules; it did not directly order their promotion.
It held that a ban on further recruitment could not, by itself, be used to treat prior appointments later regularised as recruitment or to deny consideration for appointment by transfer.

The Court said authorities could not rely after a long delay on alleged irregularity in regularisation to deny the petitioners consideration, and referred to Articles 14 and 16 in discussing career progression.
andhraPradesh.summary: On 16 September, the AP High Court ruled on temple employees’ claims for consideration for Executive Officer Grade-III posts by transfer. It directed consideration according to seniority, rather than granting automatic promotion, and addressed the distinction between recruitment and regularisation under the service rules.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Articles 14 and 16, judicial review under Article 226, and public-service promotion and seniority rules.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The order concerns appointment by transfer to Executive Officer Grade-III under the AP endowment service rules; the relief was consideration by seniority, not automatic promotion.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss the balance between recruitment controls and fair career progression in public institutions, including the importance of timely administrative action and equal treatment under Articles 14 and 16.
andhraPradesh.apLink: The ruling concerns Andhra Pradesh Endowments Department temple staff, including petitioners serving at temples in West Godavari district and Kadapa district.

national.headline: Union Cabinet raises EPFO mandatory wage ceiling to ₹25,000 per month
facts: The Union Cabinet approved raising the EPFO mandatory-coverage wage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month.
The revised ceiling is scheduled to take effect on 2026-09-17, subject to applicable statutory and scheme provisions.
Employees earning between ₹15,000 and ₹25,000 per month become eligible for mandatory coverage under the revised ceiling.
Covered employees may access EPF, Employees’ Pension Scheme (EPS) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme (EDLI).
The estimated government expenditure over five years is approximately ₹56,696 crore.
The Ministry of Labour & Employment and EPFO are to undertake statutory and administrative steps for implementation.
national.summary: The Union Cabinet approved an increase in the EPFO wage ceiling for mandatory coverage from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month. The change is scheduled to take effect on 2026-09-17 and is intended to extend formal retirement, pension and insurance-linked social protection to more workers.
national.staticLink: Social security and labour welfare; Employees’ Provident Fund and associated social-insurance institutions.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the revised ceiling (₹25,000), effective date (2026-09-17), and EPF–EPS–EDLI coverage components.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how expanding contributory social-security coverage can support worker welfare and formalisation, while considering fiscal and implementation requirements.

sources.title: Cabinet Approves Higher EPFO Wage Ceiling of Rs. 25,000, Expanding Mandatory Coverage
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Labour & Employment

national.headline: India launches Net Zero Portal and NAPCC dashboard on World Ozone Day
facts: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change held India’s national celebration of the 32nd World Ozone Day in Mumbai on 2026-09-16.
The event theme was “Global Action for a Cooler Planet”.
India’s Net Zero Portal is intended as a central repository where industries, organisations and government bodies can voluntarily register and display progress towards net-zero emissions.
The NAPCC dashboard is a digital gateway for information and tracking across national missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
The event also announced the adoption of 248 Industrial Training Institutions by 12 refrigeration and air-conditioning manufacturers to help align technician training with industry standards.
India’s reported HFC phase-down schedule under the Kigali Amendment provides reductions of 10% in 2032, 20% in 2037, 30% in 2042 and 85% in 2047 against the baseline.
national.summary: India launched a Net Zero Portal and a National Action Plan on Climate Change dashboard during its 32nd World Ozone Day national celebration. The portals are intended to support voluntary climate-progress reporting and tracking of national missions; the event also announced an industry-linked technician-training initiative.
national.staticLink: Montreal Protocol and Kigali Amendment; National Action Plan on Climate Change; climate governance and ozone-layer protection.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish the Net Zero Portal’s voluntary progress-disclosure role from the NAPCC dashboard’s national-mission tracking role.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how transparent climate-data systems and industry-aligned skills development can strengthen implementation of climate and cooling commitments.

sources.title: India reaffirms Commitment to Ozone Layer Protection and Climate Action at 32nd World Ozone Day Celebration in Mumbai
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

national.headline: PM Vishwakarma reaches 30 lakh verified registrations
facts: The PM Vishwakarma Scheme, launched on 2023-09-17, supports artisans and craftspeople in 18 identified traditional trades.
The Ministry of MSME reported 30 lakh beneficiaries registered after completing the scheme’s three-stage verification process, achieving its registration target.
Around 24.50 lakh beneficiaries had received basic skill training.
Under the credit component, 6.18 lakh beneficiaries received loans totalling ₹5,297 crore, with support of up to ₹1 lakh at a concessional 5% annual interest rate.
A total of 18.15 lakh modern toolkits had been delivered to beneficiaries.
The scheme combines recognition, skills, toolkits, credit, digital-transaction incentives and marketing support.
national.summary: The Ministry of MSME reported that PM Vishwakarma had reached 30 lakh registrations after three-stage verification, achieving its registration target. The update also reported progress in skills training, concessional credit and delivery of toolkits to traditional artisans and craftspeople.
national.staticLink: MSME development, traditional occupations, skill development, financial inclusion and livelihood promotion.
national.prelimsTakeaway: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 trades and combines certification, skills, toolkits, credit and market support.
national.mainsAngle: Examine how targeted credit, skilling and market access can sustain traditional livelihoods while improving productivity and incomes.

national.headline: Special Campaign 6 portal launched with e-waste tracking focus
facts: The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances launched the web portal for Special Campaign 6 on 2026-09-16.
The upgraded platform is intended to support monitoring across the campaign’s preparatory, implementation and evaluation phases.
A dedicated module will track e-waste, with the campaign emphasising its collection, segregation and environmentally sound disposal.
Special Campaign 6 also focuses on institutionalising cleanliness and reducing pendency in government offices.
The campaign implementation phase is scheduled for 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31.
The PIB release reported five-year campaign-wide outcomes of ₹5,000 crore earned through scrap disposal, 1,000 lakh square feet of office space freed and around 2 crore files weeded out.
national.summary: Previous: coverage concerned the preparatory phase of Special Campaign 6. Today: the campaign’s web portal was launched, with real-time phase monitoring and a dedicated e-waste tracking module; implementation is scheduled for 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-31.
national.staticLink: Administrative reforms, digital governance, records management and environmentally sound e-waste management.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Special Campaign 6 combines cleanliness and pendency reduction with scientific waste management and digital progress monitoring.
national.mainsAngle: Evaluate how digital dashboards and time-bound campaigns can improve administrative accountability, records management and public-resource utilisation.

national.headline: 20 NCC girl cadets complete the Aparajita–Parang La high-altitude trek
facts: Twenty NCC girl cadets selected from across India completed the Aparajita–Parang La 2026 expedition.
The cadets crossed Parang La Pass at an elevation of 5,578 metres, linking Himachal Pradesh’s Spiti Valley with Ladakh’s Changthang region.
The trek covered approximately 250 kilometres over 30 days, from Kibber in Himachal Pradesh to Karzok in Ladakh.
The expedition was flagged off from New Delhi on 2026-08-18 and flagged in at Karzok on 2026-09-16.
The NCC described the activity as promoting young women’s participation in adventure activities and national integration.
national.summary: Twenty NCC girl cadets completed the Aparajita–Parang La expedition, crossing the high-altitude pass between Spiti and Changthang. The approximately 250-kilometre, 30-day trek concluded at Karzok on 2026-09-16.
national.staticLink: National Cadet Corps; Himalayan and trans-Himalayan geography; youth development and national integration.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Parang La connects the Spiti Valley of Himachal Pradesh with the Changthang region of Ladakh.
national.mainsAngle: Consider how youth programmes can advance leadership and inclusion while requiring careful safety planning for high-altitude activities.

national.headline: Eighth PM Mementos e-auction launched with 1,498 items
facts: The Union Minister for Culture and Tourism launched the eighth edition of the PM Mementos e-Auction on 2026-09-16.
The auction is scheduled to commence on 2026-09-17 through the official PM Mementos portal.
The edition offers 1,498 mementos presented to the Prime Minister, including objects representing artistic traditions, craftsmanship and cultural practices.
The Ministry of Culture stated that proceeds from the auction will support the Namami Gange Programme.
The collection includes 50 identified “Hero Objects,” according to the Ministry of Culture.
national.summary: The Ministry of Culture launched the eighth PM Mementos e-Auction, offering 1,498 objects from across India. The auction is scheduled to begin on 2026-09-17, with proceeds directed to the Namami Gange Programme.
national.staticLink: Cultural heritage, traditional craftsmanship, public participation and river-conservation programmes.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The eighth edition offers 1,498 mementos, and its proceeds support Namami Gange.

international.headline: EU Commission President proposes exploring Canada as the bloc’s first associate member
facts: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made the proposal in her 2026 State of the Union address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg.
She proposed working with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to open the way for Canada to become an EU associate member; this was a proposal, not an agreed membership arrangement.
The proposed partnership agenda includes trade, technology, defence industries, the Arctic, energy, critical minerals, batteries, AI, quantum technology and cybersecurity.
The address also described plans for an EU–Canada ‘Alliance for the Future’; the speech did not establish that this alliance or associate-member status had been formally adopted.
international.summary: On 16 September, von der Leyen proposed exploring a new associate-member relationship for Canada as part of a broader effort to deepen EU–Canada ties. The proposal signals a possible expansion of the EU’s external partnerships, but no membership decision or agreement was announced.
international.staticLink: International organisations; regional integration; international trade and strategic partnerships.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Distinguish the European Union’s proposed associate-member status for Canada from full EU membership and from an adopted agreement.
international.mainsAngle: Assess how strategic autonomy, supply-chain security and geopolitical shifts are reshaping regional organisations’ external partnerships.

sources.title: 2026 State of the Union Address by President von der Leyen

international.headline: UN Secretary-General urges international cooperation on AI, climate and inequality ahead of UNGA week
facts: António Guterres made the remarks at a press briefing ahead of the 81st UN General Assembly high-level week.
He identified rapidly advancing AI, the climate crisis and deepening inequalities as major global threats requiring international cooperation.
Guterres called for AI safeguards that support safe, transparent and accountable development, with human dignity at the centre.
He reiterated calls for a two-State solution in the Middle East and a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine.
international.summary: Guterres used his pre-UNGA briefing to urge governments to cooperate on risks that cross borders, particularly AI, climate change and inequality. He also renewed calls for diplomacy and conflict de-escalation, placing multilateral cooperation at the centre of the General Assembly’s upcoming discussions.
international.staticLink: United Nations and multilateralism; global AI governance; climate change; international peace and security.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Connect the UN Secretary-General’s 16 September 2026 briefing with global AI governance, climate action, inequality and conflict diplomacy.
international.mainsAngle: Discuss the role and limits of multilateral institutions in governing transnational risks such as AI, climate change and armed conflict.

international.headline: World Ozone Day 2026 highlights the Montreal Protocol and sustainable cooling
facts: The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed annually on 16 September; the UN General Assembly proclaimed it in 1994.
The day commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer on 16 September 1987.
The UN’s 2026 theme is “Global action for a cooler planet”; 2026 also marks 10 years since adoption of the Kigali Amendment.
The Kigali Amendment provides for the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), potent greenhouse gases used in cooling.
international.summary: The 2026 observance focused on the Montreal Protocol’s ozone-protection role and the Kigali Amendment’s HFC phase-down, linking ozone policy with climate-friendly cooling. The UN highlighted the importance of expanding efficient, sustainable cooling as heat risks grow.
international.staticLink: Montreal Protocol; ozone-layer protection; Kigali Amendment; climate mitigation and sustainable cooling.
international.prelimsTakeaway: Remember 16 September, the 1987 Montreal Protocol, the 1994 UN observance, and the Kigali Amendment’s HFC phase-down.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how multilateral environmental agreements can deliver co-benefits for ozone protection, climate mitigation, public health and development.

sources.title: International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer

international.headline: Study adds heat-related labour losses to climate-cost estimates and revises agricultural damages
facts: A peer-reviewed study published in Nature Climate Change on 16 September assessed heat-related labour-productivity losses and agricultural damages for climate-cost estimates.
The researchers estimated heat-related labour-productivity damages at US$41 per tonne of CO₂ in 2025, with a reported 90% confidence interval of US$1–108.
Using updated evidence, the study revised estimated agricultural damages from US$95 to US$29 per tonne of CO₂.
The findings concern components of the social cost of carbon, an estimate used to assess the economic damages associated with carbon emissions.
international.summary: The study’s updated estimates add heat-related losses in labour productivity to climate-cost accounting while revising agricultural damage estimates downward. It highlights how scientific evidence and economic modelling can change the estimated social cost of carbon; it does not report an India-specific estimate.
international.staticLink: Climate-change economics; social cost of carbon; climate impacts on labour and agriculture.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The study estimates heat-related labour-productivity damage at US$41/tCO₂ and revises agricultural damage estimates from US$95 to US$29/tCO₂.
international.mainsAngle: Examine how the valuation of climate damages can inform mitigation policy, while accounting for uncertainty and impacts on workers and agriculture.

sources.title: New labour and agricultural damages improve climate cost estimates

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about World Ozone Day 2026 is correct?
options: It commemorates the signing of the Montreal Protocol on 16 September 1987.
It marks the adoption of the Kigali Amendment in 1994.
Its 2026 theme was “Global action for a cooler planet”, and the year marked 10 years since adoption of the Kigali Amendment.
